kapak.alt: The Eustachian tube and pressure equalization

youtube.baslik: Why do your ears feel full when a plane descends? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: As a plane descends, outside pressure rises; if the Eustachian tube cannot open to equalize middle ear pressure, the ear feels full. Swallowing, yawning or chewing gum opens the tube and eases this feeling.

instagram.kanca: Why do your ears feel full when a plane descends?
bilgiler: The Eustachian tube equalizes middle ear pressure with the outside.
As a plane descends, a tube that cannot open leaves the ear feeling full.
Swallowing, yawning or chewing gum opens the tube.

sahneler.metin: Why do ears feel *full* on landing?
cumleler: Why do your ears feel full when a plane descends?
The Eustachian tube opens to equalize middle ear pressure with the outside.
As a plane descends, the outside pressure rises.
If the tube cannot open and equalize, the ear feels full.
Swallowing, yawning or chewing gum opens the tube and eases this.
